findings.quote: Darwin and Wallace developed natural selection separately and presented papers together in $1858$.
findings.problem: Historical fact wrong as worded. Darwin and Wallace did not present the papers. Neither attended the Linnean Society meeting of 1 July 1858: Darwin was at his son's funeral and Wallace was abroad and had not been consulted. Lyell and Hooker communicated the papers and the Society's Secretary read them. Core Concept states it correctly in the passive ('Their papers were presented together'), so the trap's one-line warning, the line a student memorizes, contradicts the lesson's own teaching. The error comes from the base ('jointly presented papers') and earlier rounds did not raise it.
findings.source: Checklist B01; source policy (dates, names and historical claims need a source); Linnean Society of London, '160th anniversary of the presentation of On the tendency of Species to form Varieties' (linnean.org, 1 July 2018); Darwin Online, Darwin and Wallace 1858 paper, introductory letter communicated by Lyell and Hooker

findings.quote: A mule, from a horse and a donkey, is sterile.
findings.problem: Boundary test fails. The sentence states as a flat fact that a mule is sterile. Fertile female mules are documented (more than 60 recorded cases of foals born to mare mules). The branch lesson characteristics-of-life gives the true limit: 'Almost all mules are sterile.' The two lessons now disagree on the same fact.
findings.source: Reader rules, Added after the Sol audit (test each stated rule against a known exception); checklist B01; University extension horse resource, 'Is there a chance that a mule may reproduce if bred' (horses.extension.org); branch lesson content/lessons/science/biology/characteristics-of-life.md line 124

findings.quote: can breed with each other in nature and produce fertile offspring
findings.problem: The biological species concept, the base of the whole speciation section, rests on the word 'fertile', which the lesson never explains. The next paragraph then uses 'sterile offspring' and 'A mule ... is sterile' as the evidence of reproductive isolation, also with no meaning given, and Trap #6 uses 'hybridize' with no meaning. A Grade 5 reader who does not know that fertile means able to have offspring and sterile means unable cannot follow why a mule shows two separate species. The lesson names only genetics and heredity as a prerequisite; the lesson that does define sterile (characteristics-of-life) is not identified.
findings.source: Checklist L25; LSG Teaching completeness (explain necessary terms before their meanings are needed; a prior mention alone does not count)

findings.quote: Chance in a small group points to drift.
findings.problem: This paragraph has four sentences, over the one-to-three limit. Still open from rounds 1 to 3 in other teaching paragraphs with four sentences: the gamete paragraph, the nonrandom mating paragraph, the species paragraph, the reproductive isolation paragraph, the sympatric speciation paragraph and the adaptive radiation paragraph.
findings.source: Checklist L22a; LSG Formatting rules (paragraphs of one to three short sentences); round-3 L22a finding
